items.stem: Cursor suggests data-access code that concatenates user input straight into a SQL string. What is the main risk?

options.text: SQL injection, because untrusted input is placed directly into the query
options.rationale: Correct: concatenating user input enables SQL injection; use parameterised queries.
It may compile fine; the issue is security, not compilation.

options.text: SQL cannot be used from C#
options.rationale: C# routinely queries SQL; the issue is how input is handled.

options.text: Parameterised queries are slower, so this is better
options.rationale: Security and correctness outweigh a negligible perf concern, and the premise is wrong.

items.explanation: Correct: concatenating user input enables SQL injection; use parameterised queries.

items.stem: Which TWO tools help validate an AI change in a .NET project? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: build errors and analyzer warnings catch many issues.
Suppression hides problems rather than validating.

options.text: Deleting the tests to speed up the build
options.rationale: Removing tests removes a key safeguard.

items.stem: Why attach existing project files as context before asking Cursor to add a feature?

options.text: So suggestions follow the project's conventions and existing patterns
options.rationale: Correct: relevant context yields output that fits the codebase.

options.text: Because Cursor cannot generate C# otherwise
options.rationale: It can; context simply improves fit.

options.text: To slow the model down deliberately
options.rationale: That is not a reason to add context.

options.text: Context has no effect on output quality
options.rationale: Context materially affects how well output fits.

items.explanation: Correct: relevant context yields output that fits the codebase.
